mechanism: Label each bar with a 3-class target at horizon H: class 1 if future Close > current High (higher-high breakout), class 2 if future Close < current Low (lower-low breakdown), class 3 if future Close stays inside [Low,High] (range). Compare classifiers (AdaBoost, LDA, RF, KNN, MLP) via TimeSeriesSplit vs a binary up/down Price Target; HH/LL target is harder and less accurate than simple price-change.
data_needed: OHLC bars; look_ahead horizon (article uses 20 on Daily, EA uses configurable look_ahead); TimeSeriesSplit with gap≥horizon.

mechanism: Fit 1-feature LDA on Open only (forward SequentialFeatureSelector kept Open alone with ~−0.2% accuracy loss). Per class compute mean Open, prior P(c), pooled variance; forecast = argmax_c [x·(μ_c/σ²) − μ_c²/(2σ²) + log P(c)]. Gate entries with W1 close slope and RSI>50/<50 timing.
data_needed: Open (and High/Low/Close for labels); class counts; fetch window; iRSI; weekly closes.

mechanism: CTransEntropy measures directed information flow X→Y and Y→X. Linear TE = (1/2)·log(Var(resid_Y|Y_lags)/Var(resid_Y|Y_lags,X_lags)) via OLS (Gaussian ≡ Granger F/2). Nonlinear TE = (H(Y_{t+1},Y_past)−H(Y_past)) − (H(Y_{t+1},Y_past,X_past)−H(Y_past,X_past)) with histogram PDF bins. Difference series first for non-stationarity.
data_needed: Paired (differenced) time series matrix; lag; optional multi-lag; numBins for nonlinear; OLS residuals.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic GBM coupled walks; demo script on Crash 1000 Index M10 chart context; generic bivariate series
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a directed coupling sensor between instruments/features—who leads whom—beyond undirected correlation.
quote: If the inclusion of a secondary time series provably reduces the entropy of the target process distribution, it suggests the presence of a statistical causal influence… This reduction is referred to as transfer entropy.

mechanism: CDataWindows slices the bivariate series with winsize and winstride; TE/p/z computed per overlapping window so causality strength can appear, fade, or reverse over time—addresses non-stationary coupling.
data_needed: Same paired series; window_size; window_stride; per-window TEResult vectors.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same synthetic/demo setup; windowing optional (winsize=0 → single full series)

mechanism: Sweep lag k=1..N, compute TE both directions at each k; plot TE vs lag; true dependency lag appears as a clear peak (validated on coupled GBM with known Lag). Significance script shuffles series n times for p-value (want near 0) and z-score (want >3) at a chosen lag.
data_needed: Bivariate differenced series; NumLagsToTest; Bins; n_shuffles; chosen LagToTest.

mechanism: Entry only if (1) W1 close slope over 16 bars agrees with side, (2) ONNX forecast agrees with that side vs spot, (3) MFI(tick volume) and WPR both confirm: buy if WPR>−50 and MFI>50; sell if WPR<−50 and MFI<50—volume-flow + momentum regime gate on the neural signal.
data_needed: iMFI(VOLUME_TICK); iWPR; weekly closes; model forecast.

quote: I prefer centering them around 50. By doing so, values greater than 50 confirm bullish sentiment, while values below 50 indicate bearish sentiment. We will use the Money Flow Index (MFI) as our volume indicator and the Williams Percent Range (WPR) as our trend strength indicator.
